# GridGame Gaiden — User Stories (parity backlog)

> One line per [BIBLE](BIBLE.md) mechanic or feature. Goal: **full parity** with the GridGame2026
> bible as amended in [AMENDMENTS.md](AMENDMENTS.md).
>
> Status: **✅ verified** — a named test in `Tests/Core.Tests` or an automation-harness step
> (`tools/harness.py smoke|sweep`) demonstrates it · **🟡 partial** — built (or partly built) but no
> test/harness step asserts the behavior, or the assertion is only indirect · **⬜ planned** — not
> built. For Camp screens, harness ✅ means "the screen builds, is screenshotted and layout-audited
> in `sweep`"; the service behind it has its own line.
>
> Evidence key: test names are NUnit methods in `Tests/Core.Tests/*.cs` (last run 2026-10-09: all
> green); **soak** = `ContentAndSoakTests.Bots_play_every_stage_without_breaking_invariants` (runs
> the mechanic over real content but asserts only invariants); **smoke** / **sweep** = harness runs
> whose artifacts are in `artifacts/smoke1/` and `artifacts/sweep/`.

## Definition of Done (every story)
1. `pwsh tools/test.ps1` green (and `-Compile` for App changes). 2. Bible section updated. 3. A named
test for every rule. 4. A harness step for anything visible. 5. Glyph check green. 6. One commit at the end.

Open design questions that gate future stories live in [BIBLE §29](BIBLE.md#29-open-design-questions).


## Epic Z — Build-your-own-character redesign (parked)
- **GG-US-Z1 ⬜** As a player, I want my hero's identity to emerge from the stat and ability choices I actually make rather than a fixed class label, so a Warrior who leans into Agility feels like a different fighter and one who leans into Intelligence can eventually cast a spell like Fireball -- exact mechanism (node tree, shared ring, or pure stat-gated unlocks) is still undecided; parked to focus on core gameplay first.


## Epic W — Complete the game: content, onboarding & themes
- **GG-US-W1 ⬜** As a new player, the game introduces one camp system at a time in a natural order -- shop, blacksmith repairs, alchemy potions from looted materials, forging a weapon, then armor, enchanting armor for passive effects, then training a new skill for my bar -- each with a short guided first use, so I learn the whole loop without being dumped into every menu at once.
- **GG-US-W2 ⬜** As a player, there is enough to find, craft and fight to carry a whole campaign: 100 unique weapons, 100 unique armor pieces in named sets, 100 mechanically distinct abilities, 100 distinct enemy groups, recipes that use every material enemies drop, and enchants for armor as well as weapons.
- **GG-US-W3 ⬜** As a player, I can pick how the menus look in Settings: the current blue windows, a slate-gray theme like Chrono Trigger's default windows, or a modern dark theme like the DocFX docs sites and mindattic.com.
- **GG-US-W4 ⬜** As a new player, starting a game shows an opening crawl, a short (lorem ipsum) conversation, and a tutorial that teaches the battle controls before my first real fight.


## Epic R — Resonance-style battle rules (BRAVE, owner 2026-11-06)
- **GG-US-R1 ✅** As a player, every timeline icon flows left along one 10 s bar at Speed × 1.6 IP/tick × tempo × status and acts when it reaches the left edge, sitting at secondsUntilAct / BarSeconds, with no Zone and no crawl; casts are born at their cast time on the same bar, ties go casts first then lower id, and Slow lets a cast overtake a foe (BIBLE §2, §2.1, §2.4; GG-T286; `TimelineResonanceTests`, `Timeline_rate_is_linear_in_speed_with_no_zone_crawl`). Supersedes US-042, US-043, US-044.
- **GG-US-R2 ✅** As a player, Pushback is a keyword in seconds: an ability or item carrying it, or a hero pincer (1.5 s since GG-T306 on every foe it damages), makes the foe act later anywhere on the bar, capped at 2 s and once per foe per action, a held cast slips instead, and plain hits never push (BIBLE §2.3, §2.7, §6.7; GG-T286; `A_plain_hit_never_pushes`, `The_Pushback_keyword_pushes_its_seconds_anywhere_on_the_bar`, `One_push_is_capped`, `Validate_rejects_a_pushback_past_the_cap`, `Pincer_pushback_is_the_same_seconds_anywhere_on_the_bar_whatever_the_strength`). Supersedes US-045, US-046 and US-047 (depth × STR pushback, AGI stun).
- **GG-US-R3 ✅** As a player, the timeline reads at a glance: one track with a small diamond every second and a larger one every 5 s, every icon a diamond-masked portrait (turns) or ability icon (casts), borders enemy red, boss purple, hero cast teal, enemy charge amber and the next actor gold (gold on its tile too), a large prominence diamond at the far left showing the next actor and its seconds ("NOW" while acting), a 3 s approach glow shared by the icon and its owner's tile, and GUARD at the right end (BIBLE §2.6, §9; GG-T287; screenshots). Supersedes US-053.
- **GG-US-R4 ✅** As a player, tapping any timeline icon or the prominence diamond before a move selects that unit exactly like a board tap, with a white ring on its diamonds and a white outline on its tile, while a hold still opens the InspectCard (BIBLE §2.6, §9; GG-T288).
- **GG-US-R5 ✅** As a player, only enemies with a society or that plan ahead (tag Sentient: soldiers, mecha, goblins, orcs, frog folk, and intelligent undead such as vampires and mummies) can pincer my heroes; beasts, slimes, yetis, scorpions and mindless undead only melee; heroes always pincer (BIBLE GG-LAW-2, §1.3; GG-T289, GG-T294; `PincerEligibilityTests`). Supersedes US-012, US-027 and US-172 (Humanoid).
- **GG-US-R6 ✅** As a player, the Bestiary learns a foe by defeating it: Seen shows name, description, lore and drops; 1 defeat its Speed, 3 its HP and stats, 6 its elemental weaknesses, 10 its abilities, brain and targeting; locked rows read "???" with "Defeat N more to learn …", and the battle panel and inspect card show the same tier (BIBLE §25.11, §15.3, §9; GG-T290; `BestiaryKnowledgeTests`). Supersedes US-107 (Scan, retired), US-238, US-282 and US-292.
- **GG-US-R7 ✅** As a player, my party holds six heroes — two attackers with two supporters each — starting from three, with story recruits filling the 4th slot after Green Valley I, the 5th at Sandsea Reaches and the 6th at Frostmaw Caverns, the Veshker Ruins healer waiting in reserve, and Camp showing six in a two-column grid (BIBLE §25.14, §25.17; GG-T291; `PartyCapTests`, `StoryRecruitTests`). Supersedes US-233 (cap 4) and US-369 (party of five).
- **GG-US-R8 ✅** As a player, my Monster Tamer (Summon Circle) can Tame a wild, non-Sentient, non-boss monster, and a Dog Whistle from the Merchant can too: it turns chartreuse and fights for me on its own turn icon and AI with the Pincer keyword, fills its bond each turn, breaks free when the tame wears off unless the bond is full, and standing at a victory with a full bond asks to join as a domesticated party or reserve member (no gear, skills or tree; half XP; Lv 30 cap) (BIBLE §25.11.3, §1.3; GG-T303; `TamingTests`).
- **GG-US-R9 ✅** As a player, foes that can pincer (Sentient, and my tamed monsters on my side) engineer pincers: on their turn they swap places with monsters or heroes to close a pincer on the spot, take the end of a line an ally can close next, or slot a supporter into the chain, weighing each supporter by its own support effect; mindless beasts never swap, and every monster brings its own support (BIBLE §14.1.3, §1.3, §25.11.3; GG-T306; `PincerPlannerTests`).
- **GG-US-R10 ✅** As a player, a fast foe comes back sooner because it re-enters the bar further left (an average foe 4 s out), and every foe sits out a short recovery off the bar after it acts. The spacing between foes widens as I lower the difficulty, so I usually get a window to push back a threat, heal or shield, and when foes still cluster I squeeze in a quick move or Guard for Protection and mana (GG-T318, GG-T319, GG-T320, GG-T321).
- **GG-US-R11 🟡** As a player, I can read a Codex from Camp (the Codex row beside the Bestiary, "N new" with a New badge): places, factions, characters, foes, items, abilities, keywords and story beats unlock as I meet them, unread entries wear a New badge, a one-time Camp lesson points at the row once a stage is cleared, a "New Codex entry" toast marks a story-kind unlock in battle or the hub, and an old save back-fills what it had reached as already read (BIBLE §25.19; GG-T922, GG-T923, GG-T925, GG-T926; `CodexTests`).
- **GG-US-R12 ⬜** As a player, my heroes build two lasting bonds over the campaign: Trust, each hero's trust in me as Commander, and cohesion, how well each pair of heroes works together. Both run 0-100 in six tiers (0 / 10 / 25 / 45 / 70 / 100), and a bond never falls below the floor of the highest tier it reached, so nothing it unlocked is lost. Trust comes from dialogue choices (-10 to +10, each paid once per save), a join seed (story recruit 10, wanderer won at full Rapport 15, Summon Circle hire, freed guest or talk recruit 5) and +1 per won battle fought; cohesion from pair-scene choices and won-battle pair credits (+1 per shared pincer or heal, shield or buff on the other, capped at 5 per pair per battle). In battle Trust gives +2% crit and +2% evasion per tier and, at tier 5, Resolve (a Clutch! that survives one lethal blow at 1 HP); cohesion gives bonded pincer partners +3% damage per tier, a supporter +1 reach at tier 3+, +10% support at tier 4+ and the pair's authored Duo support at tier 5. Trust scenes play at Camp at tiers 1, 3 and 5 and pair scenes at cohesion tiers 2 and 4 (authored for the core cast of Barbarian, Cleric, Red Mage, Engineer, Knight and Sage, generic for everyone else), the highest-Trust hero voices the chapter beats, New Game+ keeps every bond, the wanderer's battle gauge reads Rapport so Trust on screen means only this bond, and every number lives in BondConfig (BIBLE §25.20; design page docs/design/trust-cohesion/; GG-T1290, GG-T1291, GG-T1292).
- **GG-US-R13 ✅** As a parent, my child's real-money spending is guarded per store login: before a wallet's first Shard Store purchase the game asks once how old the player is (Under 13, 13 to 17, 18 or older; Cancel buys nothing and asks again), each wallet has a monthly spending limit (by default $20 under 13, $50 for 13 to 17, none for adults) and a pack that would pass it is refused on the store's status line with what is left, an under-13 must answer a grown-up's multiplication question before every purchase (a wrong answer closes it and nothing is bought), and Settings > Data has a Spending limit row showing the limit and this month's spend that cycles Default, Off, $10, $20, $50, $100, No limit behind the same question unless the wallet answered adult, unlocked for the rest of that Settings visit (BIBLE §25.18.1; GG-T1437, GG-T1559, GG-T1561).
- **GG-US-R14 ✅** As a player, I can buy the starter pack, the season pass and the cosmetic bundles through the same store as the Shard packs: a product my account already owns or has hit its limit on is refused with nothing charged, a one-time purchase I made before comes back on a new phone (Android at connect, iOS through Restore purchases) without paying again, and the toast says what I got (BIBLE 25.18.1; GG-T1574, GG-T1579).

This exactly explains every observed symptom: fine on a fresh launch, breaks after enough interactions (more chances to leave one stranded), both `click`-by-name and raw coordinate `tap` equally dead (the veil, not a missing/wrong target, ate the click), and killing the process always "fixes" it (a fresh process has no orphaned veil). Fixed by tagging the veil (`confirm-veil`) and having `ScreenRouter.Go()` dismiss any stale one on every navigation (`Confirm.DismissStale()`) before proceeding. Reproduced the exact original failure (automation `newgame` after an unanswered confirm → `clicktext("Adventure")` replies `ok:true` but screen stays on `hub`) against the pre-fix build, then confirmed the identical sequence against the fixed build correctly transitions to `stages`. | GG-T67 | 2026-10-15 | fix | closed | Investigated GG-T21 with a new tools/harness.py stress HOURS command (launches once, keeps generating random battles via the randombattle endpoint, and polls the OS process directly with Popen.poll() every iteration instead of only noticing trouble through a failed/hung HTTP call). A 5h unattended run died after ~5 minutes (10 clips) -- but Player.log showed a clean Application.Quit() shutdown sequence (MindAttic.Capture CaptureRunner.OnQuitting -> physics/input-system teardown -> PlayerConnection::Cleanup), not a crash: nothing in this run's own code ever called quit. Root cause: harness.py's automation port defaulted to the same fixed 7787 for every GridGameGaiden git worktree, and launch() unconditionally quits whatever is already listening there before launching its own player -- so a second agent starting a harness run in a sibling worktree silently terminates a first agent's unrelated long-running session, with zero crash/exception trail from the terminated process's point of view. This repo explicitly expects concurrent multi-worktree agents (AGENTS.md); GG-T17's own concurrent harness run was independently found using a manually-chosen non-default port (17817), suggesting other agents had already informally worked around this. Separately, by code inspection: tools/deploy.ps1 stopped any process literally named GridGameGaiden with Stop-Process -Force, not scoped to its own worktree's Build output -- running /deploy from any worktree would forcibly kill any other worktree's running dev player too, and a hard kill leaves no app-level log output at all (no shutdown sequence, log just stops), which matches GG-T21's original symptom ("the log just stops mid-entry") even more closely than the port-collision mechanism caught live here. This doesn't retroactively prove deploy.ps1 caused the original ~1h incident -- no log survives from that session to confirm -- but it is a concrete, verified, same-shaped hazard in this repo's own tooling, strictly more likely than an undiagnosable engine crash, and worth fixing regardless. Fixed both: harness.py now derives its default automation port from a hash of the worktree's own path (GAIDEN_PORT still overrides), so sibling worktrees no longer collide by default; deploy.ps1 now scopes its Stop-Process to only processes whose exe path is under this repo's own Build\ output or the shared C:\Apps\GridGameGaiden\ deploy target. Also fixed a bug in the new stress() command itself where an HTTP call not immediately preceded by a Popen.poll() check could raise an uncaught exception instead of writing a clean crash-report.txt on an actual process death. (A) Six independent trees + toll-gated bridge (original GG-T51 draft): home tree free, off-tree nodes cost a surcharge once a points threshold is met. Rejected: felt like a tax, not organic. (C) Octagon of the game's 8 real stats (STR/VIT/AGI/SPD/STA/INT/WIS/LCK) with archetype clusters positioned by their primary/secondary stat pair, no walls between clusters: broke because forcing 8 stats onto a PoE-style shape doesn't match how PoE's tree actually works (only 3 attributes there), and produced a lopsided layout (Warrior isolated) nobody aimed for. (D) Archetype wheel, owner's own sketch: 8 'pure' archetypes (Warrior/Tank/Healer/Mage[added by Claude, not confirmed]/Debuffer/Buffer/Ranger/Thief) in a ring with 8 named hybrid nodes at the seams (Warrior x Tank, Tank x Healer, etc). Two real references surfaced but not yet applied: FF12 Zodiac Job System (12 separate per-job License Boards; a character dual-classes by picking exactly 2 of the 12 whole boards -- identity is which two boards, not where you walked) and FFX Sphere Grid (one shared lattice board everyone walks on from a different starting point, no drawn regions or walls at all -- structurally the closest real precedent to what's being searched for). Open question for next session: one shared walkable board with no drawn regions (Sphere-Grid-style), discrete per-archetype boards combined by picking two (Zodiac-style), or a named ring of pure+hybrid archetypes (owner's own wheel, option D, if refined). | GG-T98 | 2026-10-19 | fix | closed | Pincer outline drawn as a multi-tile box (owner screenshot 2026-10-19: gold outline spanning ~3x3 tiles, 'these should be impossible'). Root cause (found by reading the code): PincerFormedEvent carries only unit ids, and playback (BattleScreen.Playback.cs ~L190-215 GroupRect/DodgeBillboard/EdgeLink) reads positions from State.UnitById(id).Pos - but State is already the END-of-command state (the sim finishes before playback), so any unit that moved after the pincer in the same command (enemy turns after the hero action, knockback, displacement, later pincers in a chain, reinforcements) puts its final tile into the group rect and the outline stretches across the board. Fix: snapshot geometry at formation time in Core - add the attackers' and opponents' tiles (and footprints) and supporter tiles to PincerFormedEvent (BattleRecorder schema too, bump version if needed) and draw from those; then audit EVERY playback/view path that reads State positions for a past event (attack lunges, floats, loot bursts, death positions, cut-ins, DodgeBillboard, marks) and make each use either the event's own snapshot or the board view's playback-synced UnitView.Tile, never final State. Add a guard: a hero pincer outline is always 1 tile thick along its axis (except a 2x2 opponent's width) - assert in dev builds/tests. Evidence: a dotnet test that a pincer followed by an enemy move in the same command reports the formation-time tiles; harness screenshot of a pincer whose foe acts in the same action with a single-line outline; uicheck clean. | PincerGeometryTests.Pincer_reports_formation_time_tiles_when_the_foe_darts_away_in_the_same_command (0d030f1) |

| GG-T129 | 2026-10-19 | fix | closed | Power-ups stack on one tile (owner 2026-10-19: 'power ups can't share a space either; I see multiple pickups sitting on top of each other'). Rule: at most ONE board item (pickup or Power Amplifier / any MovableTile) per tile, ever. Found in code: pickup drops already check PickupSpotFree (PickupAt/MovableAt/TrapAt), but MaybeSpawnAmplifier (BattleRunner.cs ~L236-252, uses S.FreeForSpawn + TrapAt) ignores pickups, and MoveMovable (~L115) lets the amplifier be shoved onto a pickup tile. Fix: one 'item-free tile' check used by every item placement - amplifier spawn skips pickup tiles; an amplifier shove onto a pickup is refused like a blocked step (or define and document another rule, e.g. the pickup moves aside to the nearest free tile, never stacking); pickup drops keep their check. Also check the view: collected/expired pickups and used amplifiers must have their tokens removed, and two PickupDropped events can never draw at one tile (stale tokens look like stacking). Extend GG-T97's strict tile invariant (BattleEngine.StrictTiles / EnforceTileInvariant + the boardaudit harness check) to items: no tile ever holds two items, asserted in the strict bot soak. Tests: amplifier never spawns on a pickup; shoving the amplifier toward a pickup never stacks; a long strict soak with drops and amplifier shoves never stacks. Update BIBLE 1.1.2/1.1.3/13.3.1. | bbc8b5a |

| GG-T159 | 2026-10-21 | fix | closed | A git worktree of Unity.GridGame under D:\Projects\MindAttic.worktrees\Unity.GridGame\<ticket>\ fails tools/build.ps1 with 'Project has invalid dependencies: com.mindattic.capture/com.mindattic.telemetry ... cannot be found' -- Packages/manifest.json's file:../../MindAttic.Capture(/Telemetry)/unity/... references resolve two levels above the worktree root (D:\Projects\MindAttic.worktrees\Unity.GridGame\), which has neither sibling repo, unlike the main checkout at D:\Projects\MindAttic\Unity.GridGame\ where that same relative path lands on the real D:\Projects\MindAttic\MindAttic.Capture(/Telemetry). Found and worked around while running GG-T17's live 25-stage campaign harness in its worktree: created two directory symlinks, D:\Projects\MindAttic.worktrees\Unity.GridGame\MindAttic.Capture -> D:\Projects\MindAttic\MindAttic.Capture and ...\MindAttic.Telemetry -> D:\Projects\MindAttic\MindAttic.Telemetry (via Git Bash 'ln -s'; Windows PowerShell New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink refused for lack of admin/Developer Mode in this session), after which tools/build.ps1 succeeded cleanly. A precedent for this pattern already exists one level up (D:\Projects\MindAttic.worktrees\MindAttic.Capture and \MindAttic.Telemetry symlinks, used by repos whose worktrees sit directly under MindAttic.worktrees\<repo>\ rather than MindAttic.worktrees\<repo>\<ticket>\), but nothing had created the equivalent pair nested one level deeper for Unity.GridGame specifically, and no clone-repo.ps1/install.ps1 step sets this up automatically. Likely affects any other Unity repo with the same two-level worktree nesting and the same local-package manifest pattern (e.g. Unity.Multiplayer, Unity.Cursory, Unity.SpaceGod, UnityEve, UnitySpace -- not individually verified here). Leaving the two symlinks in place so future Unity.GridGame worktree builds don't hit this; worth a permanent fix in clone-repo.ps1/install.ps1 or the repo's own tools/unity.ps1 (e.g. auto-create missing sibling symlinks before invoking Unity) so it's not a manual per-workspace step. | 0bd43e5 |

One shared ring (not six separate trees): the 6 archetype trees (Guardian/Warrior/Ranger/Mage/Cleric/Alchemist) sit on a single unrolled ring in order Ranger-Warrior-Cleric-Guardian-Alchemist-Mage (closing back to Ranger), chosen so every seam between two ring-neighbors already matches real existing sub-archetype content: Ranger-Warrior = Duelist (STR+AGI, existing), Cleric-Guardian = Aegiswardens (WIS+VIT, existing), Guardian-Alchemist = Field Engineer (VIT+LCK, existing), Alchemist-Mage = Fieldcaster/Hexweaver-adjacent (LCK+INT, existing). Warrior-Cleric (STR+WIS) is the one genuine gap -- a Paladin/early-healer seam with no content yet. Every node on the ring is a stat pick (a primary node is +2 to one archetype's defining stat; a seam node is +1/+1 to its two neighbors' primaries); investing further along any node unlocks the ability that complements that stat combination, so a hero's identity is literally which direction and how far they walked, not a chosen class label. Deep investment along the Ranger-Warrior seam (past Duelist) resolves to the existing Shadowstep capstone kit repositioned as a Thief-flavored physical build, with no new tree needed for 'Thief'. A worked example covering the Ranger-Warrior-Cleric neighborhood was built for owner review (artifacts/Unified-Stat-Ring-Example.html, same canvas as GG-T166's superseded mockup). | GG-T168 | 2026-10-21 | feature | closed | Supersedes GG-T167; proposes resolving GG-T83 by rejecting its premise. No shared map, ring, or tree at all: AbilityDef gets a Requires field (a stat-threshold vector, e.g. Fireball: INT>=8, or a hybrid like Lay on Hands: STR>=5 & WIS>=4); every level-up grants one free point spendable on any of the 8 stats, with no node, tree, or position to walk; an ability becomes purchasable in the existing gold Learn screen the moment a hero's accumulated stats meet its Requires. There is no single authored topology to draw -- a hero's 'build' is just the history of which stats they picked, so two heroes who start identically (both reach Cleaving Strikes at STR 3) can diverge arbitrarily: one stays pure Warrior and tops out on a STR-only capstone, another spends every later point on Intelligence and eventually reaches a Fireball-tier spell at INT 8, exactly as described. A worked two-hero trail comparison was built for owner review (artifacts/Trail-Example.html, third board in the same canvas as GG-T166/GG-T167's superseded map mockups). This is a materially simpler mechanic than any node-graph: no SkillNodeDef prerequisites, no tree topology, no ring/adjacency question. If adopted it likely retires or drastically narrows GG-T74 (node expansion), GG-T78 (node-graph renderer), GG-T81/82 (region audits), GG-T135 (adjacency map), and reframes GG-T53 (no graph to render -- Learn screen just needs a 'locked, needs STR 5' state) and GG-T52 (proficiency becomes another Requires-gated unlock, not a tree node). GG-T77's GrantsStat idea is subsumed (every point is already a stat pick, no separate node needed). Needs before implementation: (1) author Requires vectors for existing abilities, grounded in current flavor (several worked examples in the mockup reuse real abilities.json entries); (2) decide whether SkillPoints survive as a separate currency from raw stat points or are unified into one pool; (3) Learn screen UI for a 'locked -- needs X' state instead of a spend-to-unlock node; (4) bot/balance support (CampRoutine stat-spend heuristics, replacing any skill-tree-spend logic GG-T54 would have needed).
